query: We are investigating a specific eutectic high entropy alloy (comprising Al, Co, Cr, Fe, Ni) that exhibits a dual-phase lamellar structure and suffers from catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility. The operating regime is room temperature uniaxial tension. Known failures include the strength-ductility trade-off and stress concentration at phase interfaces. Design constraints require maintaining the alloy composition while altering the microstructure to arrest interfacial cracking and promote uniform plasticity. Propose a high-intensity thermomechanical treatment hypothesis that could transform the lamellar structure into a patterned configuration, explain the predicted boundary conditions for success (e.g., specific temperature/pressure windows), and define a falsification experiment involving conventional hot isostatic pressing to isolate the effect of extreme pressure.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a high-intensity thermomechanical treatment (HITM) involving severe plastic deformation (SPD) followed by a controlled high-pressure annealing step will transform the continuous lamellar structure of the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy into a discontinuous, patterned 'island-in-matrix' configuration, thereby arresting interfacial cracking and promoting uniform plasticity at room temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy exhibiting a fine, continuous dual-phase lamellar structure (alternating soft fcc and hard B2 phases) with inherent stress concentration at phase interfaces leading to catastrophic cracking.
generation.intervention: A two-stage thermomechanical treatment: (1) Severe Plastic Deformation (e.g., Equal Channel Angular Pressing or High-Pressure Torsion) at room temperature to introduce high dislocation density and break lamellar continuity; (2) High-Pressure Annealing (HPA) at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 hours to induce phase rearrangement and coarsening into a patterned configuration without melting.
generation.conditions: Temperature: 1230 °C (within the eutectic stability range but below melting); Pressure: 152 MPa (sufficient to suppress void nucleation and promote phase stability); Strain: High (SPD stage); Atmosphere: Inert vacuum to prevent oxidation.
generation.structural_mediator: Dislocation-mediated phase boundary migration and pressure-induced suppression of brittle interfacial fracture, leading to the fragmentation of the continuous lamellar network into discrete, rounded B2-rich islands within a continuous fcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: The initial lamellar structure stores dislocations efficiently (evidenced by high strain hardening ratio of 16), but the continuous interfaces act as crack propagation paths. The SPD stage introduces high defect density to destabilize the lamellar coherence. The subsequent high-pressure annealing (similar to conditions in PMC5578249) promotes a topological transition where the high interfacial energy of the continuous lamellae is minimized by breaking them into isolated islands, while the applied pressure (152 MPa) prevents the formation of micro-voids and suppresses the brittle fracture mode observed in suction-assisted castings (PMC5578249), effectively mimicking the beneficial 'reticulated' or 'dispersed' phase distribution seen in other HEAs (PMC10759803) to enhance ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy will exhibit a transition from a continuous lamellar microstructure to a patterned 'island-in-matrix' microstructure. This will result in a significant reduction in catastrophic interfacial cracking, an increase in uniform elongation (ductility) at room temperature, and maintained or slightly improved yield strength due to the retained fine-scale dispersion of hard phases, effectively breaking the strength-ductility trade-off.
generation.baseline: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 alloy with continuous lamellar structure, which exhibits a high strain hardening ratio (σ_UTS/σ_0.2 ≈ 16) but suffers from low ductility and catastrophic interfacial failure due to stress concentration at continuous phase boundaries.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis holds only if the pressure window (152 MPa) is sufficient to suppress void nucleation but not so high as to induce an unwanted phase transformation (e.g., fcc-to-hcp transition observed at >6 GPa in PMC5461481). The temperature must remain within the eutectic stability range to avoid melting, as the eutectic reaction is isothermal (PMC4145285).
generation.uncertainty: It is uncertain whether the specific pressure of 152 MPa is sufficient to induce the topological 'lamellar-to-island' transition in the AlCoCrFeNi system, as the cited evidence for pressure-induced phase changes (PMC5461481) involves GPa-level pressures, whereas the HIP evidence (PMC5578249) shows phase precipitation at 152 MPa but resulted in brittleness due to grain boundary segregation. The mechanism relies on the assumption that the 'patterned' configuration will behave like the 'reticulated' Laves phase in PMC10759803 rather than the brittle grain-boundary phase in PMC5578249.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 samples: (1) Subjected to the proposed HITM (SPD + 152 MPa/1230°C/4h HIP); (2) Subjected to conventional Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) only (no prior SPD) at identical conditions (152 MPa/1230°C/4h). Perform room temperature uniaxial tensile testing on both sets.
measurements: Microstructural analysis via SEM/EBSD to quantify lamellar continuity vs. island pattern formation.
Room temperature tensile properties: Yield strength, Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS), and Elongation to failure.
Fracture surface analysis to identify crack initiation sites (interface vs. matrix).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if: (a) The conventional HIP-only sample (baseline) shows no significant microstructural change from the as-cast state (confirming HIP alone is insufficient), AND (b) The HITM sample shows a microstructure that remains continuous lamellar or forms a brittle grain-boundary network (similar to PMC5578249) resulting in elongation < 5% and catastrophic interfacial cracking, despite the applied pressure.

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: HfMoTaTiZr refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA). Intervention: Addition of 4.2 at% Cr to the nominal composition. Processing: Vacuum arc melting in an inert gas atmosphere, re-melted at least 5 times. Test conditions: Room temperature. Structure change: Formation of a Laves phase (Cr, Mo)2(Hf, Ti, Zr) in addition to the single-phase BCC structure; Laves phase forms a continuous reticulated inter-dendritic framework with a volume fraction of 3.8%. Property change: Hardness increased from 460.1 Hv 0.3 to 535.8 Hv 0.3 (56.96% higher); Yield strength increased from 1543.1 ± 40.9 MPa to 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa (207.5 MPa higher); Fracture strain increased from 11.6 ± 4.0% to 14.0 ± 2.9% (20.6% higher). Mechanism: Solid solution hardening due to Cr dissolution in BCC phase and lattice distortion; presence of hard intermetallic Laves phase; reticulated structure of Laves phase hinders crack propagation and compensates for plasticity loss. Evidence: measured. Quote: "4.2 at% Cr addition into HfMoTaTiZr led to the formation of a Laves phase, in addition to the BCC phase."

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (as-cast). Intervention: Analyzed strain hardening behavior via σ_UTS/σ_0.2 ratio. Processing: Tensile testing to determine proof stress and fracture stress. Test conditions: Room temperature. Property change: σ_UTS/σ_0.2 ratio close to 16, far beyond conventional alloys (range 1 ~ 3) and NiAl-based alloys (range 1 ~ 2). Mechanism: The very large strain hardening for the as-cast EHEA could originate from the fine regular lamellar structure that easily stores dislocations and the alternating soft fcc phases and hard B2-structured NiAl-rich phases. Evidence: measured. Quote: "the EHEA has a σ UTS /σ 0.2 (note it is the proof stress here) close to 16"

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (as-cast). Intervention: Characterized phase constitution via XRD and DSC. Processing: XRD using Shimadzu XRD-6000 with Cu target (20°–100° 2θ, 4°/min); DSC using Netzsch STA 449 F3 (10 K/min heating/cooling). Test conditions: Room temperature (XRD); Ambient to 1450°C (DSC). Structure change: fcc/B2 dual-phase constitution; single melting event in DSC confirming eutectic composition. Mechanism: Correlating the compositional information and the XRD result, the A regions shall correspond to the fcc phase while the B regions (including B II ) to the B2 phase. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the alloy is given in Fig. 3a , showing an fcc/B2 dual-phase constitution"

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (as-cast). Intervention: Evaluated castability and segregation. Processing: Preparation of ~2.5 kg ingot via conventional casting. Test conditions: Visual inspection and microstructural analysis. Structure change: Few casting defects; uniform and fine lamellar microstructure; alleviated segregation and shrinkage cavity due to isothermal eutectic reaction. Mechanism: Since the eutectic reaction is an isothermal transformation and hence there exists no a solidification temperature range, both the segregation and shrinkage cavity can be alleviated. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The bulk AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 alloy exhibited an excellent castability with few casting defects"

Intervention effect. Base system: Retained hcp CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy. Intervention: Heated to elevated temperatures at 6, 14, and 26 GPa. Processing: In situ laser heating XRD coupled with a DAC (double-sided Nd:YLF laser heating). Test conditions: Pressures of 6, 14, and 26 GPa; temperatures up to ~1,400 K. Structure change: Inverse transition from hcp back to fcc phase. Property change: Critical transition temperature for hcp-to-fcc transformation increased with pressure; at 26 GPa, transition started at ~1,400 K. Mechanism: Pressure increases the critical temperature for the hcp-to-fcc transformation; fcc is stable at high temperatures and lower pressures. Evidence: measured. Quote: "With continuous heating above ∼1,400 K at 26 GPa, the fcc phase started to gradually grow at the expense of the hcp phase"

Intervention effect. Base system: Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy buttons prepared by vacuum arc melting. Intervention: Gravity casting followed by Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP). Processing: Vacuum arc melting, gravity casting into bars, HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile tests, compression tests, creep tests at 982 °C under 200 MPa and 120 MPa. Structure change: Single-phase BCC before HIP; after HIP, a secondary HCP phase (ZrHf-rich) appeared, evenly dispersed in the matrix. Property change: Hardness increased from 323.5 ± 6.5 HV to 437.2 ± 11.6 HV; materials found to be highly brittle under tension with elongation below machine detection limit. Mechanism: The HIP process is responsible for the appearance of the HCP phase, likely due to slow cooling allowing eutectoid reaction or precipitation of HCP component from the BCC phase. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The HIP process is responsible for the appearance of a Hexagonal Close Packed (HCP) phase that is dispersed differently in these two castings."

Intervention effect. Base system: Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy buttons prepared by vacuum arc melting. Intervention: Suction-assisted casting followed by Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP). Processing: Vacuum arc melting, suction-assisted casting using a vacuum pump, HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile tests, compression tests, creep tests at 982 °C under 200 MPa and 120 MPa. Structure change: Single-phase BCC before HIP; after HIP, a secondary HCP phase (ZrHf-rich) appeared, concentrated mostly at the grain boundaries. Property change: Hardness increased from 330.2 ± 9.8 HV to 509.1 ± 13.5 HV; materials found to be highly brittle under tension with elongation below machine detection limit. Mechanism: The difference in hardness and microstructure may be related to the distribution of the ZrHf-rich phase, which is concentrated mainly at the grain boundaries in the suction-assisted casting. Evidence: measured. Quote: "Contrary to the compression properties, both materials were found to be highly brittle under tension, either during room temperature tension tests or creep tests conducted at 282 °C."

Intervention effect. Base system: Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy in suction-assisted cast condition (before HIP). Intervention: Application of Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP). Processing: HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 h. Test conditions: Microhardness testing, XRD analysis, SEM imaging. Structure change: Transition from single-phase BCC to a two-phase microstructure containing BCC and HCP phases. Property change: Hardness increased from 330.2 ± 9.8 HV to 509.1 ± 13.5 HV. Mechanism: The difference between the suction-assisted cast and the gravity cast may be related to the distribution of the ZrHf-rich phase, which is evenly dispersed in the case of the gravity casting while concentrated mainly at the grain boundaries in the case of the suction-assisted casting. Evidence: measured. Quote: "For the material that underwent HIP, the hardness was found to be 437.2 ± 11.6 HV and 509.1 ± 13.5 HV for the gravity and suction-assisted castings respectively."
